title: Light shafts are not translucent cone meshes
note: Translucent cone meshes standing in for light shafts read as pale pyramids from every wide camera; use bloom on the emitter or a soft sprite.
intent: A translucent ConeGeometry under a lamp reads as a pale pyramid — from a wide camera a street of them looks like a row of tents. If the shaft is worth having, get it from the light itself: bloom on a bright emitter, a soft radial sprite billboarded to the camera with additive blending and a fade at the top and bottom, or a real volumetric pass. If none of those fit the budget, no shaft at all is better than a cone.

check.js: objects().filter(o => o.isMesh && o.geometry && o.geometry.type === 'ConeGeometry' && o.material && (o.material.transparent || o.material.blending === 2)).length === 0
check.note: No translucent cone meshes stand in for light shafts — they read as pale pyramids ('huts') from every wide camera. Use bloom on the emitter or a soft sprite instead.

port: The lighting facet removes any cone mesh under a lamp and puts the glow on the emitter instead.
